## add read-base split columns to error.parquet

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-13
```

### description

The user asked whether the `--error-out` Parquet can also carry
`to_a`/`to_c`/`to_g`/`to_t` and whether that is cheap. After a feasibility
answer, the user chose the 4-column option (no `to_n`). `to_x` counts
in-region substitutions at each 1-based position whose read (destination)
base is x.

### result

1. Implemented `to_a`/`to_c`/`to_g`/`to_t` columns in `error.parquet` (9-column schema).
2. Answered the cost question: negligible CPU, small memory, modest file growth.
3. Documented the N-base semantics in `docs/usage.qmd`.

### change

## assess forward/reverse strand read-count output

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-20
```

### description

The user proposed adding a parameter that writes a file counting reads on
the forward and reverse strands, and asked whether it is cheap and whether
the design is sound. I read this as a request for an evidence-backed
assessment (plus my own position, with room to refute) before any
implementation.

### result

1. Answered: cheap — measured ~25 ns/read (5 ms per 200k reads) for the is_reverse counter; all candidate loops already visit every mapped record.
2. Answered: agreed on the metric, with a placement pushback — qc-summary columns (~20 LoC) beat a new annotate output file (~60 LoC) unless the pipeline runs annotate only.
3. Answered: verified pysam.flagstat on a 50%-reverse BAM reports no strand split, so flagstat cannot replace the feature; samtools view -c -f/-F 16 covers only global counts.
4. Answered: pinned semantics — mapped records only; include secondary/supplementary alignments so forward + reverse equals total_reads.

### change

Files:
- updated: `docs/misc/next_and_recommendation.qmd`, `docs/misc/requirements_audit.qmd`

Packages/Environments: None

## confirm strand placement; assess annotate stats-flag removal

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-20
```

### description

The user confirmed qc-summary as the home for the forward/reverse strand
read counts, then asked whether the four annotate stats flags
(--fl-stats/--tc-stats/--ap-stats/--nb-stats) should be deleted since
qc-summary appears to subsume them.

### result

1. Answered: placement confirmed — forward/reverse counts will be columns in qc-summary.parquet.
2. Answered: recommended NOT deleting now — fl/tc/ap stats use the same shared judgement functions as qc-summary (redundant), but --nb-stats has no qc-summary equivalent.
3. Answered: deletion breaks three surfaces at once (CLI flags, output files, Python API StatsCollector export); recommended deprecate-then-remove if pursued.

## explain qc-summary column computation basis

```
level: low
date: 2026-10-20
```

### description

The user asked whether the qc-summary output columns are produced by
counting the tags that annotate wrote, or by recomputing each judgement
per read.

### result

1. Answered: recomputed per read — qc-summary never reads sam-tagger tags; it uses CIGAR, read seq, and minimap2's cs tag through the same shared functions annotate uses.
2. Answered: flagged one definitional asymmetry — error numerator is inner-region-gated, aligned_bases denominator is the full cs span.

### change

None

## confirm tag-plus-stats computes each read once

```
level: low
date: 2026-10-20
```

### description

The user asked whether, when a *-stats flag runs together with its
--add-* tag flag, the per-read judgement is computed twice (once for the
tag, once for the stat).

### result

1. Answered: computed once — verified empirically for FL (300 records, --add-fl + --fl-stats both on, 300 judgement calls) and by code structure for TC/AP/NB.
2. Answered: stats piggyback on the tagging pass at zero extra per-read compute; only the Parquet write is additional work.

None

## assess stripping fl-tc-ap columns from qc-summary

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-20
```

### description

The user proposed resolving the redundancy the other way around: delete
the fl/fl_pct/on_target/on_target_pct/ap_* computations from qc-summary,
because --add-* plus --*-stats on annotate is the dominant use case.

### result

1. Answered: recommended AGAINST stripping — annotate stats Parquets carry (seq_name, count) only, so fl_pct/on_target_pct would lose their only home.
2. Answered: qc-summary's stated purpose is the joined digest (README); stripping pushes consumers to glue 4 files plus per-ref totals by hand.
3. Answered: for the full QC picture, annotate-stats + error-stats and annotate + qc-summary cost the same 2 BAM passes; the difference is output shape, not pass count.

### change

- updated: `docs/misc/next_and_recommendation.qmd`, `docs/misc/requirements_audit.qmd`

## assess read-length and DM distribution outputs in qc-summary

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-20
```

### description

The user proposed adding per-reference read-length and DM-tag length
distributions to qc-summary, encoded as a JSON object (pos->count) or a
dense array (index=pos) inside the Parquet, and asked for agreement with
room to refute.

### result

1. Answered: agreed on the metrics; refuted JSON encoding via live demo — polars cannot point-lookup numeric JSON keys (json_path_match Eof) and json_decode needs a pre-declared dtype.
2. Answered: soft-refuted the dense-array encoding — workable but index semantics stay implicit and every plot/aggregate unnests back to relational.
3. Answered: recommended a long-format optional side output (seq_name, metric, value, count), the existing TypedStats house pattern.
4. Answered: flagged the denominator decision — primary-only (each read once) vs all-mapped (strand-column consistency).

### change

Files:
- updated: `docs/misc/next_and_recommendation.qmd`, `docs/misc/requirements_audit.qmd`

## assess smoothed deletion attribution in error.parquet

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-20
```

### description

The user proposed a smoothed_deletion column in error.parquet: a deletion
inside a reference homopolymer run is positionally ambiguous, so spread the
count uniformly over the run (ref TTTAAATTT, read TTTAATTT -> 1/3 A at each
of positions 4,5,6). Asked whether it is cheap and whether I agree.

### result

1. Answered: agreed — a live demo shows the SAME deletion placed at position 4 by one alignment and 5 by another, so per-position counts carry an alignment-convention artifact.
2. Answered: cheap in compute (O(run length) per deleted base) but not free in interface — run detection needs the reference sequence (cs ':' encodes lengths only); error-stats gains --fasta.
3. Answered: pinned semantics — per-base detection over the maximal same-base reference run; region-clipped mass; sum(smoothed)==sum(deletion); first Float64 column in error.parquet.

### change

Files:
- updated: `docs/misc/next_and_recommendation.qmd`, `docs/misc/requirements_audit.qmd`

Packages/Environments: None

n/a here; null-fallback chosen) for homopolymer-smoothed deletion

## assess depth total and rate columns in error.parquet

```
level: medium
date: 2026-10-20
```

### description

The user proposed adding a `total` column to error.parquet matching
`samtools depth -J -a -a`, plus per-position rate columns
(insertion/deletion/mismatch/to_a/to_c/to_g/to_t/smoothed_deletion), and
asked whether it is cheap. The user directed verification via a samtools
source clone rather than web docs.

### result

1. Answered: samtools semantics verified from cloned source (bam2depth.c line-cited) — -J counts deletions, -a -a zero-fills all contigs, default filter drops unmapped/secondary/dup/qcfail.
2. Answered: cheap — the depth difference-array over cs ops is O(ops) per read (2 dict updates per op), no fasta needed; rates are 8 divisions per position at write.
3. Answered: flagged that -J is exactly what keeps deletion_rate <= 1, and that exact samtools parity requires no secondary/qcfail/dup records (our universe keeps numerator/denominator consistent).

### change

Files:
- updated: `docs/misc/next_and_recommendation.qmd`, `docs/misc/requirements_audit.qmd`

Git (outside this repo):
- cloned samtools (shallow) to /bioproj/tools/github/samtools for source verification
